purpose: Ball VS Space Inventory and Store visual direction exploration before implementation and workflow comparison
status: Colorful arcade direction chosen; revised desktop mockups await user review. No target lock or runtime validation.
feedback: It's not bad, but it can be done a bit better to make it look like Roblox UI.
visualDecisions: Simpler navy panels and cobalt header
Dark outlines and modest corner radii
Chunky cyan actions, quieter preview actions
Existing ball and icon identities retained as references
limitations: Concept images, not screenshots of implemented changes
Generated sprites are approximations of the canonical artwork, not replacement runtime assets
Desktop only; responsive phone target remains to be designed and checked
No economy, additional kits or new gameplay systems implemented

prompts.status: First concept, superseded after user feedback
prompts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create a high-fidelity desktop Roblox game Inventory redesign for Ball VS Space in a polished COLORFUL ARCADE direction. This is a proposed visual target, not an implemented screen. Produce one complete front-facing screen, landscape 1536 x 1024, with crisp legible typography. No device frame, annotation arrows, or presentation-board layout.

Input image 1: current Inventory screenshot, used for the real UI content, existing game context, and interaction structure; redesign the appearance and proportions.
Input image 2: existing ball artwork atlas, used as the identity reference. Retain these exact simple ball designs and recognizable colors/silhouettes, without inventing equipment or ball types.
Input image 3: existing icon atlas, used for category and axe artwork.

Visual direction: premium playful arcade UI built from plausible Roblox GUI shapes and image assets. A substantial deep-navy window with a rounded 18px blue rim, subtle bevel and drop shadow; layered navy/slate cards; bold friendly rounded white headings; clean highly readable supporting type with minimal outline. Bright yellow, turquoise, purple and coral accents. Color belongs to artwork, the active tab, selected state and primary action. Avoid four equally loud huge tab slabs. No neon sci-fi HUD, ornamental metal, glass dashboard, space ships, planets or excessive particles. Keep a narrow dim blurred blue lobby backdrop around the window. The interface fills nearly the entire frame.

Header: small Inventory box icon, large readable "Inventory"; below it "12 ball appearances". A compact rounded red close button with a clear white X at upper right.
Navigation: four horizontal, generously spaced illustrated tabs "Balls", "Explosions", "Flyers", "Fusion". Balls has a yellow selected fill; the other three have dark fills and colorful small existing icons. Tabs have readable labels and consistent height, not giant artwork.

Body: two columns. Left roughly 66 percent is a scrollable 3-column collection grid; right roughly 30 percent is a substantial selected-item detail card. Six whole cards are visible in two rows, with a scrollbar indicating the remaining collection, no invented pagination or search.
Row 1: "Verity Ball" yellow smile sphere; "Axe Ball" slate sphere with orange stripe and axe; "Poison Spike Ball" smooth lime sphere.
Row 2: "Burst Ball" orange sphere with pale plus; "Cell Ball" translucent green concentric sphere; "Vampire Ball" red sphere with two white fangs.
All ball names large and readable, especially the longer name; all cards use equal padding. Art occupies around 60 percent of each card. Use softly lit dark inset wells and integrated name areas, no thin tiny blue label strips.
State example: Verity has a small gold check badge reading "Equipped". Axe is selected with a strong cyan outline and subtle cyan inset light, visually distinct from the equipped badge. Other cards remain neutral, without rarity tiers or stats.

Right detail panel: small cyan "SELECTED" label, bold "Axe Ball", large preview of the actual Axe Ball and its weapon. Small informational chip "Anchor kit". Description, exact text: "Spins an axe, widening its territory." Below a divider: "Equipped: Verity". Bottom contains one large tactile cyan "Equip" button with white bold type, raised edge, and ample padding. No duplicate equipped claim for Axe, no purchase control.
Keep the mockup attractive through hierarchy, spacing and consistent shapes, not through replacing the existing assets with unrealistically complex artwork.
Constraints: preserve the existing four categories and selection/equip structure. All artwork is cosmetic; do not add new ability mechanics, rarity, prices, currencies, trading, fusion actions, search, sorting, favorites, upgrades or locked-item mechanics. Only use the exact requested visible text.

Use case: ui-mockup.
Revise the attached Ball VS Space Inventory concept to feel much more like a polished, actual ROBLOX GAME ScreenGui, following the user's feedback that it looks good but needs to look more like Roblox UI.
Output a single front-on complete desktop Inventory screenshot, landscape 1536 x 1024, crisp text and clean layout.

INPUTS:
Image 1 is the previous generated Inventory concept to revise. Keep its content, game assets, three-column collection and selected-item panel. Its over-glossy neon treatment is what must change.
Image 2 is the actual current Roblox game screenshot, for authentic in-game context, simpler rendering language and existing structure. Improve its typography and hierarchy.
Image 3 is the original ball atlas. Preserve these simple game sprite designs.
Image 4 is the original icon atlas, for the actual axe and category symbols.

STYLE CHANGE:
Make this look like a realizable Roblox GUI with flat Frames, UIStroke, modest UICorner, TextLabels and simple ImageLabels. Solid midnight-blue panel; 4px almost-black outer stroke; rounded corners around 10px; a small offset dark shadow. No luminous outside border. Flat cobalt-blue header band, modest cyan accents. Bold friendly rounded white game typography with a clean DARK OUTLINE; use simple highly legible white/pale-blue body text. Chunky rectangular buttons with gently rounded corners, solid saturated fills and a short darker bottom edge. NO neon bloom, glossy plastic reflections, glowing platforms, sci-fi frame, multiple nested decorative rims, glass UI, metallic surfaces or dramatic lighting. Aim for a polished Roblox arcade collection menu, not a mobile gacha game. Clean spacing; minimum 24px readable card names in the rendered image. Existing ball sprites are vivid, softly shaded, but not newly modelled photoreal collectibles. Behind the menu, a narrow subdued blurred glimpse of the existing blue blocky Roblox lobby.

LAYOUT:
A centered window using about 92% of frame width and 90% height, enough breathing room. Compact header about 100px high: white "INVENTORY" left, small subtitle "12 ball appearances", square coral-red close button with a clear white X top right. Do not use a giant cube app-logo.
Four category tabs in one tidy row, roughly 68px tall: "Balls", "Explosions", "Flyers", "Fusion", with modest original icons beside labels. Active Balls is golden yellow; inactive tabs are muted blue with colorful icon accents. Tabs are not huge billboards.
Collection takes about two-thirds of main body and selected-item card one-third. Left grid shows six consistent cards in 3 columns x 2 rows, slim scrollbar for the rest. Each card is one simple slate-blue tile, almost-black outline, large art centered and a clearly readable name below. Avoid layers of inset frames.
First row: "Verity Ball" yellow smiley sphere, "Axe Ball" slate sphere with orange stripe and axe, "Poison Spike Ball" smooth lime sphere.
Second row: "Burst Ball" orange plus sphere, "Cell Ball" concentric pale-green sphere, "Vampire Ball" red sphere with two white fangs.
Verity has a compact gold check badge reading "Equipped" at top of its tile. Axe selected state is a SOLID cyan outline, no glow. No rarity, stats, item counts, locks or new mechanics.

Right side: a simple slightly lighter navy detail panel, no excessive nested borders. Small cyan "SELECTED" above "Axe Ball", large original Axe sprite including axe, small "Anchor kit" pill. Description exactly: "Spins an axe, widening its territory." Natural two-line wrapping, comfortably readable. A subtle separator then "Equipped: Verity". At bottom a wide chunky cyan "Equip" button, bold white dark-outlined text and dark bottom edge. Equip should look tappable, not luminous.

Preserve all six named cards, all four category tabs, and correct equipped-versus-selected distinction. Do not add weapons or cosmetic designs, prices, purchase controls, extra features, mascot, slogan, unrelated HUD, or fake Roblox branding. Only the specified text.

Use case: ui-mockup.
Create the matching STORE screen for the attached revised Ball VS Space Inventory mockup. The user chose colorful arcade, then asked for a more authentic Roblox game UI feel. This Store must belong to exactly the same UI family as image 1. One finished front-facing desktop screen, landscape 1536 x 1024, crisp legible text, no device frame or design-board annotations.

INPUTS:
Image 1: approved-for-exploration visual direction, the revised Inventory mockup. Match its solid navy/cobalt panels, dark outlines, modest corner radii, chunky white outlined rounded type, compact buttons and blurred blue Roblox lobby background. It is a style reference, not a Store layout.
Image 2: actual existing Store screenshot, the content/interaction reference. Preserve its four categories, four offered items, balances, view/preview actions and collection spotlight. Redesign the presentation.
Image 3: existing ball sprites; keep identities exactly.
Image 4: existing icons; use its coin, blue gem, events squares, red-ball category shape from the UI, explosion cloud, UFO, balloons and blue parasol.

STYLE:
Polished real Roblox ScreenGui appearance: simple flat Frames, UIStroke, 10px rounded corners and a slight offset shadow. Midnight navy window, solid cobalt header, almost-black substantial outlines. Friendly white rounded display font with dark outline; clean readable light-blue supporting text. Subtle surface gradients only. Keep the actual simple sprite artwork, not photorealistic models. NO exterior cyan glow, neon bloom, glossy plastic reflections, glowing pedestals, glass, sci-fi ornament, floating holograms or metallic trim. Narrow dimmed blocky blue lobby visible behind the menu. Consistency with image 1 is essential.

LAYOUT:
Centered window about 92% of frame width and 90% height. Header: bold "STORE" at left, small subtitle "Explore the collection". At upper right, two compact navy pills with coin icon and "0", blue gem icon and "0", followed by a square coral-red X close button. Currency balances are passive, not prominent purchase controls; no plus buttons.
Navigation row: "Events", "Balls", "Explosions", "Flyers". Small category icons at left of large readable labels. Events selected with solid cyan-blue fill; remaining tabs muted navy with colorful icons. Same tab height and type scale as Inventory.

CONTENT:
A section heading "Collection picks" and a small gold "Free collection" badge.
Below, four equal cards across:
1. "Laser Ball": original smooth violet sphere with pale-lilac rim and small highlight. Action "View Ball".
2. "Ray Ball": original orange sphere with pale yellow band around its middle and pale yellow central disk. Action "View Ball".
3. "Colorful Balloon": original cluster of purple, cyan, pink, yellow and lime balloons with strings and red bow. Action "Preview".
4. "Blue Parasol": original cyan/blue triangular umbrella with gray shaft. Action "Preview".
Each is one flat slate-blue tile with dark outline, generous art well, distinct readable name, and one chunky integrated action button at bottom. Cyan buttons for View Ball, quieter purple-blue for Preview. Text is comfortably large. Do not add rarities, prices, sales, timers, exclusivity badges, purchases or new behaviors.

Below cards a wide purple/slate collection spotlight banner, about a quarter of the main content height. Left: small "COLLECTION SPOTLIGHT", strong two-line headline "Find your next favorite", and readable subtitle "12 ball appearances · All free". Right: an attractive compact grouping of the existing Laser, Ray and Orbit sprites, purple largest and the other two slightly smaller, against simple flat diagonal purple bands. Existing art only; no wings, bundle accessories or new ball effects. Do not add a new button or call it a bundle.
Bottom small but readable footer: "All ball appearances are free. No purchase needed."

Keep the hierarchy calm enough to scan: artwork and item names first, then actions. Header and tabs must not consume most of the screen. Preserve the same Roblox-native, colorful arcade treatment as revised Inventory. Only requested text. This is a mockup, not a claim that an economy or daily rotation exists.
